alignments.note: Postpositive δέ rendered by the clause-initial But.
First member of the εἴτε … εἴτε correlation, rendered whether.
Inflected passive with its subject and auxiliary as helpers; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb.

Verbless clause with a prepositional predicate. The clause expresses no subject, so under rule 68 the supplied it as well as the copula ride with the predicate, and rules 53 and 62 put both on the preposition; rule 17 heads on for. Word order beside the supplied it is not what licenses a helper.

Article displaced by the possessive your, which belongs to the genitive ὑμῶν (rule 20). ὑμῶν is free — its only English is that possessive — so rule 76's availability test leaves rule 20 proper in force.
Genitive pronoun rendered by the possessive.
Plain noun-to-noun correspondence.
Coordinating καί rendered and.
Plain noun-to-noun correspondence; the case is already carried by the expressed ὑπέρ.
Second member of the correlation; the juncture or is the obligatory English helper introducing it (rules 29 and 88), so it is not added.
Subject and auxiliary are helpers; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb.
Second verbless clause; supplied it is rides with the preposition exactly as in the first, under rules 53, 62 and 68.
Article displaced by the possessive your on ὑμῶν (rule 20), as at s005.
Genitive pronoun rendered by the possessive.
Plain noun-to-noun correspondence.

Second attributive article governing an expressed head noun (παρακλήσεως) with a participle following: rule 31's τὴν δύναμιν τὴν ἐνεργουμένην → the power that worketh, the same lexeme. The relativizer belongs to the participle and the article realizes nothing.
Attributive participle rendered as a finite relative clause; which is its helper, headed on the verb (rule 31).
Preposition rendered by in.

One Greek noun rendered by an English adjective-plus-noun phrase. The Greek is anarthrous, so the supplied *the* is an ordinary rule 51 helper on the phrase. Rule 91's operational test decides the head, and the corpus line is unbroken: ὑπομονή heads on *patience* in all twelve of its units, and the related ὑπομένω on *patiently*, so *patient* is the word the corpus spends on this stem. The corpus contains exactly one *endur-* token and it is spent on a different lexeme, ὑποφέρω → *endureth* at 1PE.2.19, which is rule 91's own discriminator — the test is which word the corpus spends on this Greek word, not which reads as the phrase's formal English noun, and rule 17 forbids choosing *enduring* merely because it is that noun. Rule 84's line applies: with the corpus 14 to 0 the head is not in doubt.

Article with its case preposition riding along (rule 21), headed on the per rule 17. The intensive αὐτῶν is not a demonstrative and does not empty the article under rule 38; the ASV writes the determiner out.
Attributive αὐτός in the identity sense, rendered same.
Plain noun-to-noun correspondence.
Relative pronoun rendered which, with no supplied word expanding it (rule 77 not in question).
Adjunctive καί rendered also; the ASV's reordering across the pronoun is permitted by rule 15.
Expressed subject pronoun.
Finite verb rendered suffer, its subject standing on the expressed ἡμεῖς.

review_notes: Reviewed against the contract and left unchanged; all 26 source and 36 target IDs are partitioned exactly once.

Both ὑπέρ phrases are verbless clauses with a prepositional predicate and no expressed subject, so rule 68 puts the supplied subject as well as the copula on the predicate and rules 53 and 62 put both on the preposition. The recurring failure rule 53 names — reading the copula off English word order onto the supplied it — is what this refuses.

Both τῆς before παρακλήσεως are emptied under rule 20 by ὑμῶν, which rule 76's availability test confirms is free: its only English is the possessive. The third article (s016) is emptied by rule 31, whose worked example τὴν δύναμιν τὴν ἐνεργουμένην → the power that worketh is this same participle.

s019 the patient enduring is the only head genuinely in question. Rule 66 heads on the noun where the noun glosses the lexeme, and enduring does; rule 91's corpus test is the competing reading, since the ASV's standing gloss for ὑπομονή is patience and patient is its adjectival form. A chapter with corpus access should check what 2CO and its neighbours spend on ὑπομον- and may prefer patient; recorded medium either way.
s020 of the follows rule 21 rather than rule 38: αὐτῶν here is the identity intensive, not a demonstrative, and the construction requires the article, which the ASV writes out as the.
